title: ぜひ — by all means, definitely
summary: An adverb that strengthens a wish or a request: “by all means / I really want to.” It is used together with ～たい, ～てください, and ～てほしい. It expresses a strong feeling that you want something to happen.

patterns.gloss: ぜひ + ～たい: I really want to ～
ぜひ + ～てください: please do ～ by all means

body.p: With ～たい, ぜひ shows how much you want to do something. With ～てください, it turns an invitation or a suggestion into a warm, strong one, as in ぜひ遊びに来てください. It is often used for hospitality.
ぜひ always goes with a wish, an invitation or a request. It is not used for plain facts (ぜひ行きました is wrong) or for orders. For must-do duties, use 必ず.

examples.ja: ぜひ私（わたし）の国（くに）へ遊（あそ）びに来（き）てください。
examples.romaji: Zehi watashi no kuni e asobi ni kite kudasai.
examples.tr: By all means, please come visit my country.

examples.ja: 新（あたら）しい店（みせ）ができたら、ぜひ行（い）ってみたい。
examples.romaji: Atarashii mise ga dekitara, zehi itte mitai.
examples.tr: When the new shop opens, I definitely want to go.

examples.ja: この料理（りょうり）はおいしいので、ぜひ食（た）べてください。
examples.romaji: Kono ryōri wa oishii no de, zehi tabete kudasai.
examples.tr: This dish is delicious, so please do try it by all means.

pitfalls: Do not use it with plain statements or in the negative: ぜひ行きませんでした is wrong.
It is not for orders or duties. For “must”, use 必ず or ～なければならない.
